item.title: Using the CKBHash Function in CKB Development (1 posts)
item.description: CKBHash is a term you might see within the various CKB libraries, and for basic usage it’s abstracted away for you. For more advanced lock design you need to understand what it is and where it is commonly applied. We put together a quick guide to explain how these conventions work. Using the CKBHash Function in CKB Development When building smart contracts on CKB you are free to use any cryptographic function that you wish to use. However, many of the system scripts and within the commonly used libraries rely on Blake2b. In this post we describe some of the specific CKB conventions on how to use it properly with the existing foundations. In most cases, you will rely on libraries that...

item.title: Understanding CKB Lock Value Relationships (1 posts)
item.description: When you work with the CKB Cell Model, there are a lot of different lock values and the terminology can be confusing at first. Even for a seasoned developer, how all these values fit together is often overlooked. This is why we are sharing this guide to explain it in simple terms. Understanding CKB Lock Value Relationships In CKB smart contract development, it is important to understand how different lock-related values connect to each other. These values form a chain of cryptographic relationships that are used throughout smart contract development for purposes such as ownership verification, address generation, and cross-referencing between different scripts. item.title: Design Patterns: UTXO Transfers Using the Cell Model (1 posts)
item.description: How to transfer assets with the Cell Model is a surprisingly complex subject because of the state rent requirements. We wanted to share a guide on seven patterns (both current and future) that developers should understand. Design Patterns: UTXO Transfers Using the Cell Model This document explores different patterns for transferring digital assets between two parties using the Nervos CKB Cell Model. While focused on the CKB blockchain, these patterns may also apply to other UTXO blockchains that implement state rent. item.description: Question Time Xiaomao noir1920×1080 710 KB Noir CKB is a developer toolchain that connects the Noir programming language (for writing zero-knowledge proofs) with the Nervos CKB blockchain. In simple terms: Imagine you want to keep a secret number (like a private score or balance) stored on a blockchain, where only you should be able to update it, without ever revealing the number itself. Noir CKB is an experimental way to write private logic in the relatively friendly Noir language, and safely enforce it on CKB. item.title: ReuseLoop: Tracking reusable packaging lifecycles on CKB Testnet (1 posts)
item.description: What happens to a reusable package as it moves through borrowing, return, and reuse—and what can CKB actually verify about that journey? ReuseLoop is a CKB Testnet prototype that records an item’s administrator-authorized state changes: AVAILABLE → BORROWED → RETURNED → AVAILABLE. CKB records application state and authorized transitions. Physical handoffs, returns, cleaning, and inspections happen off-chain and are not proven by the chain. item.title: [DIS] Fiber Claim Cell: Async Receive and On-Chain Claims for Fiber LSPs (1 posts)
item.description: I’d love to hear from more of the Fiber community! The goal of Fiber Claim Cell is straightforward: give existing LSPs an on-chain claim option when a receiver has no usable channel, rather than build another LSP service. The prototype flow has run on testnet; real-wallet validation, safety hardening and an independent audit are still part of the proposed work. If this is something you’d like to see built, please like this post to show your support. If you build a wallet or run an LSP, which receiving scenario would make this useful to you? Questions and concerns are just as welcome. I’d rather address them now, while the scope is still open for discussion.

item.title: Spark Program 申请 | CellCat（暖暖猫舍）：能熔回 CKB 的链上基因猫 (1 posts)
item.description: ( English below ) 这是什么？为什么要做在 CKB 上？ CellCat 是一个跑在 CKB 上的全链上基因猫小游戏，玩法很简单：领养 → 配对产蛋 → 等出块孵化 → 挂单交易 / 熔猫。 选 CKB 带来的特性： 猫有真地板价：每只猫都是一个真实的 Cell，喂食就是往里存 CKB；不想玩了随时“熔猫”，Cell 里的 CKB 全退回钱包。 不存图，链上算基因：每只猫只存 32 字节 DNA（显性+隐性基因），繁殖先产蛋、到指定块高取区块头做随机源，链上重算 DNA 防作弊。 无托管原子交易：用 sale-lock 挂单，买家付够 CKB 直接换锁成交，卖家随时撤单，不需要把猫转给平台托管。 零门槛：接入 JoyID，不用装插件背助记词，打开网页就能玩。 目前已经做完的部分（本地 Devnet 已跑通） 4 个 Rust 合约（cat-type、egg-type、sale-lock、config-type）：纯手写字节布局和 ckb_std::syscalls，避开了 riscv64imac 原子指令的坑。 跨端基因库：Rust（no_std）和前端 JS 逐字节一致，有 82 条自动化校验向量。 合约测试：ckb-testtool 写了 20 多个正常和异常用例（防改 DNA、冷却、次数上限、繁育费、区块头、挂单少付/错付等），已全过。 移动端网页：猫舍、繁育、集市、明信片生成和基础社交交互在本地 devnet 上已经能玩。 图片1440×2802 387 KB 开发规划 第 1...

item.title: Fiber LSP: Running Channels on the Server, Signing in the Wallet (1 posts)
item.description: Following up on my earlier note, @joii2020: the proposal is now live — Fiber Claim Cell! I’ve narrowed it to one piece existing LSPs could reuse: an on-chain claim option for receivers without a usable channel. The goal is to complement hosted LSP delivery, not build another public LSP. The prototype flow has run on CKB testnet; real-wallet validation, security hardening and an independent audit are still part of the proposed work. I’d love your take on where this would fit in the hosted delivery flow. If other wallet developers or LSP operators see a use for it, please share your use case or support in the proposal thread — that would really help shape the funding discussion.

item.title: CKBA Membership Process (1 posts)
item.description: Contributing Member applications for the 2026 Q4 GA CKBA accepts Contributing Member applications year-round.
